sourcedFrom: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) (2023 (date code 06/23 on the back cover))
cleanIntro: Savage prints one manual for the Model 334, and every step below is quoted from it. The 334 is a bolt-action rifle with a detachable single-stack magazine, a three-position safety button behind the bolt, and a Bolt Release Lever that lets the bolt come out of the back of the receiver. Savage's strip takes the bolt out, then the two action screws, the stock and the trigger guard. Savage's own limit is plain: nothing is taken apart beyond those disassembly sections, and the trigger screw is factory set and never forced.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, safety button to Safety On
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep your finger out of the trigger guard for all of unloading. Pull the safety button back to the middle position, Safety On, where only the white dot shows and the trigger is blocked. Do not use the fully rearward Bolt Locked position here: it locks the bolt shut, and you need the bolt to open to unload.
steps.quote: Always point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep your finger out of the trigger guard. Push the safety button to the "Safety On" position
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Unloading the Rifle, p.17

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Press the magazine release button at the front of the magazine well with a finger and pull the magazine away from the rifle. Take it out before you touch the bolt, so working the bolt cannot feed another cartridge into the chamber. Set the magazine aside, away from the rifle.
steps.quote: While pressing the magazine release button in front of the magazine well with your finger, pull the magazine away from the firearm.
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Unloading the Rifle, p.17

steps.title: Bolt handle up, bolt back until it stops
steps.action: Lift the bolt handle and draw the bolt all the way back until it stops. Pulling it back extracts any cartridge or fired case from the chamber and throws it out of the receiver, so keep your face clear of the ejection port and be ready to catch it.
steps.quote: Lift the bolt handle and pull the bolt back until it stops.
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Unloading the Rifle, p.17

steps.title: Chamber checked by eye and by finger
steps.action: Look into the chamber and feel it with a fingertip to confirm there is no cartridge or empty case left in it. Check the magazine well as well. If a cartridge or case is stuck in the chamber, Savage says to take the bolt out, leave it out, and contact Savage or a qualified gunsmith before the rifle is used again.
steps.quote: In order to be sure that there is no loaded or empty cartridge in the chamber, check the chamber visually and by hand.
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Unloading the Rifle, p.17
steps.warn: Check the chamber and magazine at least "twice" before sliding the bolt assembly forward and closing it. Otherwise, any cartridge in the chamber can be fired.

steps.title: Bolt handle fully up, bolt fully back
steps.action: With the magazine out and the chamber proved empty, rotate the bolt handle upward until it stops, then pull it rearward until the bolt stops against the bolt stop. The bolt has to be all the way back for the release to let it go.
steps.quote: Rotate the bolt handle upward until it stops and pull it rearward until the bolt stops.
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Disassembly of the Rifle, Removing the Bolt Assembly from the Rifle, p.18

steps.title: Bolt Release Lever pressed, bolt drawn out
steps.action: Press and hold the Bolt Release Lever on the receiver and pull the bolt straight out of the back of the receiver. Set the bolt down where it cannot roll or pick up grit. With the bolt out you can look through the bore from the back of the receiver to the muzzle.
steps.quote: While pressing the Bolt Release Lever, pull the bolt out of the receiver
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Disassembly of the Rifle, Removing the Bolt Assembly from the Rifle, p.18

steps.title: Front and rear action screws out, 5 mm hex
steps.action: With the bolt open or out and the magazine removed, turn the front and rear action screws counterclockwise with a 5 mm hex wrench until they are free. Use a wrench that fits the screw heads fully so they do not round. Keep both screws together.
steps.quote: Unscrew the front and rear action screws by rotating them counter clockwise using a 5mm hex wrench
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Disassembly of Stock and Trigger Guard, p.19

steps.title: Stock pulled straight off the barreled action
steps.action: Pull the stock straight away from the barrel and receiver. Do not lever or twist it off, which can bind the trigger in its cutout or mark the inletting.
steps.quote: Remove the stock by pulling it straightly from the barrel and receiver.
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Disassembly of Stock and Trigger Guard, p.19

steps.title: Action screws and pillars pushed out of the stock
steps.action: Push the action screws and their pillars firmly out of the stock. Keep each pillar with its screw so the same pair goes back into the same hole.
steps.quote: Remove the action screws and pillars from the stock by firmly pushing them
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Disassembly of Stock and Trigger Guard, p.19

steps.title: Trigger guard out, front end first
steps.action: Pull the front end of the trigger guard outward from the stock first, then work the rear part out until the guard comes free. It goes back in the opposite order, rear first.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger guard by pulling the front end outward from the stock
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Disassembly of Stock and Trigger Guard, p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Bolt out, stock off, action screws, pillars and trigger guard out. That is as far as Savage lets an owner take the Model 334. Leave the trigger and its fixed, factory-set trigger screw alone, and do not take the bolt apart.
steps.quote: Never disassemble your firearm beyond the instructions included in the disassembly sections of this manual.
steps.cite: Model 334 Instruction Manual — (06/23) Rev 01 (printed on the back cover) — Assembly of the Rifle, warnings, p.21
steps.warn: The Trigger Screw is fixed and is factory set, do not try to force it.

deepAbsentReason: The book's disassembly ends on p.19 with the bolt out and the stock, action screws, pillars and trigger guard off. On p.21 it says 'Never disassemble your firearm beyond the instructions included in the disassembly sections of this manual.' and 'Never manipulate internal components beyond what you are instructed to do in this manual.', and it publishes no deeper procedure.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Magazine and bolt out of the rifle before you start
Solvent on a bore brush of the right size, then push it from the chamber end out of the muzzle a couple of times; let the brush exit the muzzle before pulling it back
Clean patches from the chamber end out of the muzzle, taking each dirty patch off before pulling the rod back, until a patch comes out clean
Wipe solvent residue off the muzzle with a clean rag
One lightly oiled patch through from the chamber end
Do not run the rod in from the muzzle end; it can damage the crown and degrade accuracy
Do not leave oil in the chamber or bore; residual oil can cause over-pressure or a blockage

cleaning.name: BOLT ASSEMBLY
tasks: Clean every surface of the bolt assembly with solvent, a small soft bristle brush for stubborn deposits
Dry it with a clean patch or lint-free rag
A mild coat of gun oil over the assembly

cleaning.name: BARREL & RECEIVER EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe every reachable surface of the barrel and receiver with a lint-free rag soaked in solvent; a soft bristle brush for the corners
Wipe all the solvent off with a clean, dry rag
Gun oil on a clean rag, applied lightly; leave no excess oil

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Solvent on a clean rag over the outside of the magazine and the follower, then dry it straight away
A light coat of gun oil on every surface of the magazine you can reach

cleaning.name: STOCK
tasks: Normally a wipe with a clean, dry rag is enough
After hunting or shooting in rain, clean the stock completely

reassembly: Safety button on Safety On, chamber empty, magazine out. Lay the stock onto the barreled action, lining the trigger up with the rear of its cutout.
Fit the trigger guard rear end first, then rotate the front end into the stock.
Put the action screw pillars into the stock, then the action screws.
Tighten the front and rear action screws carefully with a 5 mm hex key; Savage recommends 60 inch-pounds.

Check the chamber and bore are empty and free of oil and debris. With the safety on Safety On, line the bolt handle up at 2 o'clock with the slot in the receiver and slide the bolt in; pressing the Bolt Release Lever helps it go. Release the lever and listen for the click as it engages the bolt body.
Slide the bolt forward until it stops and turn the handle down until it will go no further.
fncheck: With no ammunition in the rifle or magazine and the muzzle in a safe direction, work the bolt fully back and fully forward and down several times; it should run smoothly and close with the handle fully down. With the handle down, move the safety button through all three positions and confirm each one: fully forward shows the red dot, the middle shows only white and blocks the trigger, and fully rearward also locks the bolt so the handle will not lift. If anything binds, or the safety does not work in every position, do not load the rifle; take it to a qualified gunsmith or Savage Arms.
